thread.title: Amazon Earnings Give a 4% Boost to Shares

author: Jon Swartz
title: Amazon Earnings Give a 4% Boost to Shares
text:
By Jon Swartz July 26, 2018 4:28 p.m. ET Illustration: Getty Images/iStockphoto Amazon (AMZN) hauled in less revenue than expected last quarter--and forecast fewer sales than analysts anticipated for the current quarter--but the stock rose as much as 4% as earnings surpassed forecasts.
The tech behemoth rang up $5.07 in earnings per share, with revenue of $52.9 billion. In the same quarter a year ago, the company earned 40 cents per share on $37.95 billion in revenue.
Analysts surveyed by FactSet expected earnings of $2.48 per share on revenue of $53.4 billion for the three months ended in June.
Amazon offered third-quarter guidance for revenue of $54 billion to $57.5 billion, falling short of the $58.04 billion consensus estimate from analysts surveyed by Capital IQ .
Daniel Ives , head of technology research at GBH Insights , said in a note to clients the "massive beat on the margins/EPS and healthy profitability outlook going forward will be a major positive that investors will focus on when digesting results."
"In a nutshell, after the Facebook debacle last night we believe the Street will be somewhat relieved to see Amazon deliver another strong quarter as the secular
tailwinds on both the consumer and enterprise fronts are massive for Bezos & Co. going forward," said Ives, who maintains a "Highly Attractive" rating on the stock with a price target of $2,000.
The profitable quarter--Amazon's largest, at $2.5 billion--came even though the Seattle-based company invested heavily in fulfillment centers, new stores, and pricey content deals. The results, showing strength in Amazon's e-commerce, content, and cloud services businesses, illustrate the broad reach of the company's operations.
Amazon, which accounts for about half of the online retail sales in the U.S., has "the most robust and durable growth outlook" of any company in the FAANG group, which includes Facebook (FB), Apple (AAPL), Netflix (NFLX), and Alphabet's Google (GOOGL), Canaccord Genuity analyst Michael Graham wrote in a note to investors this month.
At $904.3 billion as of Thursday's close, its market valuation was second only to Apple's among publicly traded companies in the U.S., as the tech giants race to become the first $1 trillion company.
Amazon's e-commerce revenue will jump 28% to $394.23 billion this year, and its digital ads sales will surge 58% to $3.37 billion as it becomes more of a threat to Alphabet and Facebook, according to eMarketer .
Amazon Prime membership will reach 88.7 million viewers in the U.S. in 2018, up 12% from a year ago. That's about 44% of the so-called over-the-top video market--streaming media content delivered via the internet to consumers that bypasses traditional broadcasters-- compared with a 74% share for Netflix, eMarketer said.
